---
description: rules_add as the model is told it - what the tool does, and what each of its arguments is.
doing: adding a row to one of the rules' tables
arguments:
  table: "What the row is: a skill, a class, a trait (a feat, a race, a class feature), a condition, a size, a weapon, an armour, a creature or a difficulty."
  id: "The row's key in its table: letters, digits, underscores, dots and hyphens."
  row: "The row's columns, by name. Each table's own columns are named in the answer when a row lacks one."
---
Adds a row to one of this world's tabletop rules tables, or changes the one with that key, as a feat, a weapon or a creature the story needs and the rules do not have yet. The row is checked against the table's columns and the world's own checks before anything is written, and a row that cannot work is told with why. The table is changed in the world's next revision and this chat moves to it from its next turn; the world's other chats stay on the revision they play. A world whose draft in Build holds changes not kept yet, and a chat on an older revision than the world's newest, are told so and left alone. One Undo (the Upgrade's) takes it back.
